claims.explanation: RITA binds p53 and disrupts the p53-MDM2 interaction, reactivating wild-type p53 to induce apoptosis. Selectivity is therefore expected in lines with wild-type TP53 and intact p53 pathway signaling, while TP53-mutant or p53-pathway-inactivated lines are protected. The observed sensitive lines are enriched for wild-type TP53 (e.g., ZR751, GP2D, HEC265, K029AX) and the resistant lines are enriched for TP53 mutations or p53-pathway defects, consistent with a p53-dependent mechanism.

features.basis: RITA requires wild-type p53 to induce apoptosis; TP53-mutant lines are largely resistant
MDM2 overexpression increases p53 degradation and may limit RITA response
CDKN2A loss is enriched in resistant lines and may reflect p53-pathway/ARF dysfunction
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling but also may sensitize to p53-mediated apoptosis in some contexts
PIK3CA mutations are enriched in sensitive lines and may cooperate with p53 activation
BRAF-mutant lines appear in both groups but some sensitive melanoma lines carry BRAF mutations
EGFR-mutant lung lines are among sensitive lines, possibly reflecting oncogene addiction
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive colorectal and pancreatic lines
ARID1A mutations are present in several sensitive lines and may alter chromatin response to p53
SMARCA4 mutations appear in resistant lines and may impair p53 transcriptional activity
ATM loss may impair p53 activation and DNA damage responses
NFE2L2 mutations appear in resistant lines and may protect against oxidative stress-induced apoptosis
